property_summary: For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's entire balance to the provided recipient (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and recipient's balance increases by the withdrawn amount); the mutant that instead sends funds to msg.sender (owner) breaks this when the provided recipient != owner.

For any caller and any recipient, after the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero and the provided recipient (not necessarily the caller) receives the funds; the mutant that sends to msg.sender (owner) violates this whenever recipient != owner.

For every nonzero contract balance and any recipient address, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds leave the contract); the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender instead can leave the contract balance unchanged for some inputs (when transfer to msg.sender fails), so this universal 'balance becomes zero after owner withdrawAll' is broken by the mutant for some adversarial recipient behaviour.

For every adversarial recipient contract that reverts on receiving ETH and for every nonzero initial balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the call should revert (so the transfer to the recipient fails) — the mutant that redirects the transfer to msg.sender (owner) will succeed instead and therefore not revert for some inputs, distinguishing the mutant from the reference.

For every recipient contract that always reverts on receiving ETH and for any nonzero contract balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the reference C's call will revert (because it attempts to transfer to the recipient) while the mutant that instead transfers to msg.sender (the owner) will not revert for some inputs, so the universal property is: 'owner calling withdrawAll(revertingRecipient) always reverts' — the bug breaks this by sending to owner instead of recipient.
